results.name: Biceps Curl Cable
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing a low cable pulley. Hold the handle attached to the low pulley with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands at shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended and elbows close to your body.
Curl the handle upwards towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain an upright posture and avoid leaning back during the curl.
Focus on squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement to enhance muscle activation.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
results.description: Biceps Curl Cable is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Biceps Curl Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, placing the middle of the resistance band under your feet. Hold the handles of the band with your palms facing forward and arms fully extended down by your sides.
Keeping your elbows close to your torso, slowly curl the handles of the band towards your shoulders by bending your elbows.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the curl, holding for a brief moment to maximize contraction.
Slowly lower the handles of the band back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain proper posture and avoid strain.
Do not use your shoulders or swing your body to lift the band; focus on isolating the biceps.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
results.description: Biceps Curl Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Biceps Curl to Shoulder Press Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, placing the middle of the resistance band under your feet. Hold the handles of the band with your palms facing forward and arms fully extended down by your sides.
Perform a biceps curl by bending your elbows and bringing the handles of the band towards your shoulders, keeping your elbows close to your torso.
From the biceps curl position, rotate your wrists so that your palms face forward, and press the handles of the band overhead by extending your arms fully.
Lower the handles back to the starting position by reversing the steps. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Exhale as you press the band overhead and inhale as you lower it back down to maintain steady breathing.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the shoulder press to keep tension on the muscles.
results.description: Biceps Curl to Shoulder Press Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Forearms.

results.name: Cable Twisting Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand slightly sideways to a low cable pulley and hold the handle with one hand using a neutral grip. Keep your elbow close to your side and your arm fully extended.
Curl the handle toward your shoulder while rotating your forearm from a neutral grip into a supinated grip as your elbow bends.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement with your palm facing upward while squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position while rotating your forearm back to a neutral grip. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Keep your elbow close to your side throughout the movement and avoid using momentum to curl the weight up.
Perform the movement smoothly to maintain constant tension throughout the exercise.
Finish each repetition with a fully supinated grip to maximize biceps contraction.
Inhale as you lower the handle and exhale as you curl it upward.
results.description: Cable Twisting Biceps Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Shoulders.

results.name: Concentration Curls Dumbbell
instructions: Sit on a bench with your legs spread apart. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand and rest your right elbow on the inside of your right thigh.
Let the dumbbell hang down towards the floor with your arm fully extended.
Curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder by contracting your biceps, keeping your elbow stationary and close to your thigh. Squeeze the biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arm. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm.
tips: Focus on squeezing the biceps at the top of the movement to maximize muscle activation.
Ensure your back remains straight and avoid leaning back as you lift the weight.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form and without straining.
results.description: Concentration Curls Dumbbell is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Drag Curl Dumbbell
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip (palms facing up). Let your arms hang straight down by your sides.
Begin by dragging the dumbbells upward along your torso by bending your elbows and pulling them back, as if you are zipping up your jacket.
Continue lifting the dumbbells until they reach chest height, focusing on squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the descent. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on the mind-muscle connection, feeling the contraction in your biceps throughout the movement.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form without straining.
Avoid using momentum; perform the exercise in a slow and controlled manner.
results.description: Drag Curl Dumbbell is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Drag Curl Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a resistance band under your feet. Hold the handles of the band with both hands, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows close to your body and your back straight. Start with your arms fully extended down at your sides.
Curl the handles up by dragging your elbows along your torso, keeping them close to your torso, until your hands reach chest level.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you curl the handles up and inhale as you lower them back down.
Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on engaging your biceps throughout the movement.
results.description: Drag Curl Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Curl Alternating
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inwards (neutral grip).
Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl one dumbbell up towards your shoulder, rotating your wrist so your palm faces upward (supinated grip) at the top of the curl.
Hold the top position for a brief moment, ensuring you squeeze your biceps, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, rotating your wrist back to the neutral grip.
Repeat the curl with the other arm, alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movements in a controlled manner, avoiding any jerking or swinging.
Ensure your elbows stay close to your body and do not flare out during the curl.
Keep your wrists straight and avoid excessive bending.
results.description: Dumbbell Curl Alternating is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Curls
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inwards (neutral grip).
Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders, rotating your wrists so your palms face upward at the top of the curl.
Hold the top position for a brief moment, ensuring you squeeze your biceps.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, rotating your wrists back to the neutral grip, maintaining control throughout the movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movements in a controlled manner, avoiding any jerking or swinging.
Ensure your elbows stay close to your body and do not flare out during the curl.
Keep your wrists straight and avoid excessive bending.
results.description: Dumbbell Curls is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Seated Zottman Curl
instructions: Sit upright on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand by your sides using an underhand grip.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl both dumbbells toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms.
At the top, rotate both hands into an overhand grip, then slowly lower the dumbbells until your arms are fully extended.
Rotate your hands back into an underhand grip at the bottom, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms still.
Curl the dumbbells without swinging your shoulders or leaning forward.
Keep your wrists straight and rotate back to an underhand grip only after fully extending your arms.
Exhale as you curl the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Dumbbell Seated Zottman Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.
